userStories.title: The GitHub Actions excerpt leads with error annotations
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Lead GitHub Actions repair excerpts with bounded error annotations while preserving the end of the job log.

**Motivation** — The 200-line tail excerpt shows none of it.

**Approach** — **Annotation excerpt (part of defect 1).** For a GitHub Actions job whose log has lines containing `##[error]` (anywhere in the line: the API prefixes each line with a timestamp), the excerpt is an annotation block followed by a tail block:

```
GitHub Actions error annotations:
<up to CI_ANNOTATION_LINES lines containing ##[error], in log order>

Log tail:
<the end of ciExcerpt(log)>
```

The annotation block, header line included, is at most `CI_ANNOTATION_CHARS` characters; lines that would pass that bound are dropped from the end of the block, and a single first line longer than the bound is cut to it. The tail block gets the remaining budget: it is `ciExcerpt(log)` cut from its start so the whole excerpt is at most `CI_EXCERPT_CHARS` characters. A log with no `##[error]` line, and every GitLab trace, keeps the excerpt `ciExcerpt(log)`.

Read through US-001's sanitized readJobLog rather than introducing another subprocess or moving redaction after bounds. Preserve the last non-empty log line even with a trailing newline.

**Scope** — In: annotation selection, annotation/tail character budgeting, GitHub Actions excerpt composition and regression preservation of unavailable-log results. Out: log API and sanitization (US-001), CI wait/skip (US-003), interactive log views (US-007/008). Excerpt anchoring on language- or tool-specific failure markers (for example a test runner's fail lines) is not done; only GitHub Actions `##[error]` annotations lead the excerpt.

**Interface** — Reuse the upstream constants verbatim:
```ts
export const CI_ANNOTATION_LINES = 20;
export const CI_ANNOTATION_CHARS = 2_000;
```
Existing `ciExcerpt(log)` and `CI_EXCERPT_CHARS` remain the fallback and total excerpt budget; no new public signature is specified.

[unit] For a GitHub Actions log with no line containing ##[error], the failed check's excerpt equals ciExcerpt(log).

userStories.title: The GitHub CI wait settles, and a repair needs a readable log
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wait for remaining GitHub checks after an observed failure and skip CI repair when no failed-check log can be read.

**Motivation** — The real failures were a test timeout in an untouched package (a flake: green on the re-run) and an `e2e` regression the agent never saw, because the wait had stopped before `e2e` finished.

**Approach** — **CI wait (defect 2).** In `waitForChecks` for GitHub, a poll with a failed bucket and at least one bucket that is neither failed nor passed is a *failing* poll: not terminal, and not passed through the mergeability read (a failed check keeps its meaning, as today). The rules, in order:
1. A later readable poll decides as today: all passed is `green`, a failed bucket with none pending is `failed`, a conflict is `conflicting`. A re-run that turns everything green ends `green`.
2. Error polls count toward the existing unreadable-poll run (`CI_ERROR_POLL_LIMIT`). When the run reaches the limit, the wait ends `failed` if a failing poll was observed for this head since the wait started, and `unavailable` otherwise (today's behaviour).
3. At the deadline, when the latest readable poll was failing, the wait ends `failed` with a detail naming the failing checks and saying how many checks were `still pending`; this wins over the errored-poll `unavailable` rule, because a failed check was observed for this head.
GitLab is unchanged: its pipeline status turns `failed` only when the pipeline is done. `readChecksOnce` (one read, used by the bot) is unchanged. Every `waitForChecks` caller inherits the change: the workflow publish (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`), `nax workflow promote` (`src/cli/workflow-promote.ts`) and the bot fix report (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`).

**No evidence, no repair (defect 3).** When every failed check of the repair read has `logUnavailable`, the CI repair decision returns no repair and the ledger says why. The draft PR stays as published. `src/workflow/feature-steps.ts` is 582 lines against the 600-line limit; the change there stays within it.

When every failed check of a CI repair read has `logUnavailable` → no CI repair round; ledger note `CI repair skipped: no failed check's log could be read (<names>)`. Check the existing empty-list case separately; mixed readable/unreadable evidence still yields one finding per failed check. Preserve existing progress lines, heartbeat cancellation, abort, head binding and unreadable-poll reset behavior. Shared classifyGh/pollOnce logic must not change readChecksOnce's fail+pending verdict. Use the scripted virtual clock and ledger harness, not real sleeps.

**Scope** — In: GitHub failing-poll wait/history/deadline classification and all-unreadable repair skip. Out: excerpt generation (US-001/002), provider transport and PR bindings (US-011/012). The GitLab CI wait is unchanged; a GitLab pipeline reports `failed` only once it has finished. `readChecksOnce`, the bot's one-shot CI read, is unchanged. A skipped CI repair is not retried later in the same run.

**Interface** — Existing `waitForChecks` / `CiWaitResult`, `ciRepairDecision` and `readCiFailuresForRepair` retain their external contracts. Consume US-001's `FailedCheck` target: `{ name; url?; excerpt; logUnavailable?: true }`.

userStories.title: The pr and checks tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose bound-PR metadata and its current head's complete check listing through the provider core.

**Motivation** — The repair agent spent 38 minutes reconstructing CI locally, asked for the log through `RequestCapability` (refused, as designed), and ended with an empty commit to re-trigger CI.

**Approach** — Tool contracts:
| Tool | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `pr` | none | number, state, draft flag, base ref, head ref, head sha, URL and title |
| `checks` | none | one line per check of the PR's current head: id, name, status, the conclusion when completed, and the URL when present |

Every tool takes the bound PR from `resolveRef`, which the provider calls at most once per successful resolution (a rejected resolution is retried on the next call). Every input is validated before mode selection and before any forge call.

Everything a tool returns that came from the forge (PR fields, check names, log lines, comment bodies) is rendered inside one `markdownFence` block per tool result; the lines nax writes itself (headers, counts, footers) stay outside it. Every tool builds its result with `fitToolResult`, which fits whole entries (a log line, a check line, a comment) to the run context's `maxBytes` instead of cutting the finished string: it keeps the header, as many whole entries as fit from the kept side (`"end"` for the `log` tail view, `"start"` for every other view), always closes the fence, keeps the footer, and adds a `[truncated: <k> entries not shown]` line after the footer when it dropped any. A single entry that does not fit alone is cut on a code-point boundary.

A forge read inside a tool throws → the tool returns `isError` with the first non-empty line of the error's message, redacted.

Add pr-tools.ts and register localName pr/checks in the upstream provider. Resolve the bound ref with the shared successful-resolution cache. Read PrInfo through _forgeToolsDeps.readPrInfo on each relevant invocation; checks then passes its headSha to _forgeToolsDeps.listHeadChecks, binding deps/cwd throughout. This must exercise the real provider handler chain, not merely direct listing helper tests. Error content for a message `
boom
more` is exactly `boom`; token-bearing messages are redacted.

**Scope** — In: pr/checks handlers, namespace advertisement, metadata and check entry rendering and non-throwing errors. Out: provider core (US-005), log tool (US-007/008), writer tools (US-009/010), dispatch/binding (US-011/012). The `pr` tool does not return the PR description body. Logs or checks of any head, PR or repository other than the bound PR's current head are not readable.

**Interface** — Consume the existing/upstream `readPrInfo(ref, deps, cwd)`, `listHeadChecks(ref, headSha, deps, cwd)` and `ProviderTool.run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: ToolRunContext): Promise<ToolResult>` contracts through _forgeToolsDeps. No additional public function signature is prescribed.

userStories.title: The log tool reads a check of the PR's head
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read and tail only a job belonging to the bound PR's current head, validating input and caching completed job logs per provider.

**Motivation** — An agent needs to search the log, not read its tail; that is what the `log` tool does.

**Approach** — Tool contract: `log` input is `check` (string of digits, or an integer, required), `search` (non-empty string), `from` (integer >= 1), `lines` (integer 1..500, default 200); output is a header naming the check, its status and a `showing lines <x>-<y> of <n>` line; then the numbered log lines.

Every input is validated before mode selection and before any forge call.

The log's lines are its text split on newline, with one empty final element after a trailing newline not counted. Every emitted log line is prefixed with its 1-based line number and cut to `FORGE_LOG_LINE_CHARS` characters. The `check` must be the id of a check in `listHeadChecks` for the PR's current head sha. A completed check's log text is read once per provider and reused; a check that is not completed is read on every call. The tail view fits to `maxBytes` with `keep: "end"`; the page and search views with `keep: "start"`.

Implement input validation for all four fields in this story, even though page/search selection is delivered by US-008. With neither search nor from, tail returns the last lines (default 200). Read current PrInfo and head checks through _forgeToolsDeps before authorizing the id and before consulting completed-log cache; no cached log may bypass head membership. Use US-001's readJobLog result and never another subprocess path. A non-completed job is partial, and an in_progress check's output says `job still running: this log is partial`. Render numbered lines and forge-derived check text inside the upstream single-fence fitter, with nax-owned showing/count lines outside.

Failure handling: `log` names a check that is not a check of the PR's head → `isError` naming the id and pointing to `nax-forge__checks`; no log read. `log` names a check with no job log (a non-Actions GitHub check) → `isError` saying the check has no job log. `log` input invalid (wrong type, out of range, empty `search`, missing `check`) → `isError` naming the field; no forge call. A failed readJobLog returns isError holding its reason.

**Scope** — In: log handler/advertisement, complete input validation, current-head check authorization, per-provider completed-log cache, tail selection and partial-log notice. Out: page/search algorithms (US-008), listing implementation (US-004), API log implementation (US-001), dispatch/binding (US-011/012). The `log` tool does not read the output text of non-Actions GitHub checks; that text stays in the CI repair excerpt. Logs or checks of any head, PR or repository other than the bound PR's current head are not readable.

**Interface** — Reuse upstream exports verbatim:
```ts
export async function readJobLog(ref: PrRef, checkId: string, deps: ForgeDeps, cwd: string): Promise<JobLogRead>;
export const FORGE_LOG_DEFAULT_LINES = 200;
export const FORGE_LOG_MAX_LINES = 500;
export const FORGE_LOG_LINE_CHARS = 1_000;
```
The tool is a ProviderTool with localName `log`; all forge calls use `_forgeToolsDeps`.

userStories.title: The log tool's page and search views
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add page and literal-search views to the authorized log tool, preserving original line numbers and bounded fenced output.

**Motivation** — Even a readable log did not help: in the failed `test` job's 24 155-line log the failing test sits at line 2 845, followed by about 19 000 lines of other packages' output that a monorepo task runner prints after the failure.

**Approach** — `log` modes compose in this order: `search` present selects search mode (case-insensitive literal substring, no regex; `from` and `lines` are ignored); otherwise `from` present selects page mode (`lines` lines from `from`); otherwise tail mode (the last `lines` lines). The log's lines are its text split on newline, with one empty final element after a trailing newline not counted. Search mode returns at most `FORGE_LOG_MAX_MATCHES` matching lines plus a `<shown> of <total> matches` line. Every emitted log line is prefixed with its 1-based line number and cut to `FORGE_LOG_LINE_CHARS` characters. The `check` must be the id of a check in `listHeadChecks` for the PR's current head sha. A completed check's log text is read once per provider and reused; a check that is not completed is read on every call. The tail view fits to `maxBytes` with `keep: "end"`; the page and search views with `keep: "start"`.

Every input is validated before mode selection and before any forge call.

Extract pure view selection/rendering into log-view.ts and extend log-tool.ts using the upstream validation, head authorization and log cache. A page starting after the log end contains no numbered lines and reports `showing lines 0-0 of <n>`. Apply literal case-insensitive matching to full sanitized log lines, count all matches, show the first 50, and only then apply per-emitted-line character limits and whole-entry byte fitting. A supplied invalid from remains invalid even when search selects the view. Use markdownFence through fitToolResult; never slice a finished fenced result.

**Scope** — In: search/page composition, matching/counting, page bounds, line numbering/line cap, start-kept byte fitting and regression preservation of the existing default tail view. Out: log API (US-001), provider core (US-005), changes to log authorization/cache contracts (US-007), PR/session binding (US-012). Log search is a literal substring match; regular expressions are not supported.

**Interface** — Reuse upstream constants:
```ts
export const FORGE_LOG_DEFAULT_LINES = 200;
export const FORGE_LOG_MAX_LINES = 500;
export const FORGE_LOG_MAX_MATCHES = 50;
export const FORGE_LOG_LINE_CHARS = 1_000;
```
Inputs: `check` (string of digits, or an integer, required), `search` (non-empty string), `from` (integer >= 1), `lines` (integer 1..500, default 200). No new public view-function signature is prescribed.
